Subject: SCCs / module selection for EU->US patient data transfers

Hi Soojin,

Quick question as we're consolidating the DPA for our upcoming pilot: Borealis will be a controller for patient-identifiable telemetry collected in the EU and intends to send de-identified and potentially re-identifiable telemetry to Redwood for enrichment/analysis. Our legal team wants clarity on which 2021 SCC module Redwood intends to sign (controller->processor vs processor->processor), and whether you accept the UK Addendum for UK-origin data.

Can you confirm:
- Which SCC module Redwood will use for EU controller -> Redwood (US) transfers?
- Whether Redwood will execute the UK Addendum and any supplementary risk notes for healthcare data?
- Any constraints on onward transfers / subprocessors we should be aware of?

We're aiming to finalize the DPA + SCCs next week if possible — appreciate a clear recommendation and any redlines we should expect.

Thanks,
Emma Clarke

Subject: Re: SCCs / module selection for EU->US patient data transfers

Hi Emma — thanks for the note and the diagram. Short answer up front: for the flow you described (Borealis = controller; Redwood = processor) we recommend Module 2 (Controller -> Processor) for EU transfers, plus the UK Addendum for any UK-origin data.

Rationale and key points:
- Module selection: Module 2 is the standard 2021 SCCs module for controller->processor relationships. It fits the described flow and aligns with our standard DPA obligations.
- UK Addendum: We will accept and sign the UK Addendum as provided by Borealis (we have a small, standard set of edits for clarity around subprocessors and audit logistics).
- Healthcare sensitivity: Because telemetry can be sensitive in your use case, we recommend including the optional supplementary security notes (we've attached a short memo with recommended TOMS and a proposed carve-out for restricted processing).
- Onward transfers / subprocessors: Redwood restricts onward transfers to subprocessors only for operational delivery. We publish a subprocessors page and will provide a 30-day notice for any new subprocessor that would receive EU personal data. We can accept a contractual restriction that prohibits onward transfers outside: (i) adequacy countries; (ii) transfers covered by SCCs + UK addendum; or (iii) transfers to subprocessors listed in schedule X.

Next steps: Markus and Laura are looped for legal/privacy signoff — I've attached a short memo and our draft DPA for your review. If this approach works, we can prepare the final DPA + SCCs + UK Addendum and send for signature by early next week.

Regards,

--

Thanks Soojin — quick legal note.

I agree Module 2 + UK Addendum is the correct baseline for Borealis' described controller->processor flow. A couple of nuance items to call out for healthcare data:
- Supplementary provisions: add explicit reference to our TOMS in the Annex and include a short schedule (we have a template clause referencing encryption-in-transit and at-rest, access controls, and incident response SLA).
- Optional module augmentation: while Module 2 covers the core transfer obligations, consider an explicit language bullet in the DPA restricting certain categories (e.g., genetic/clinical trial identifiers) from being processed without prior written approval — this avoids unanticipated high-risk processing.
- Audit rights: Borealis may request on-site audits for processor obligations. We can accept remote audits annually; on-site will require coordination and scoped notice.
- Subprocessor carve-outs: propose Redwood's standard 30-day notice + opt-out right for high-risk subprocessor additions.

I'll coordinate with Laura to finalize the small privacy edits; Soojin, please confirm whether we should attach our UK Addendum redline or return the Borealis form with comments.

-Markus

Subject: Final: Module 2 + UK Addendum + DPA timeline

Emma — thanks for the follow-ups. Apologies for the short delay; final position below.

1) Onward transfer restriction: Redwood can agree to a contractual limitation that onward transfers are limited to: (a) countries with an adequacy decision, (b) transfers under SCCs (including UK Addendum where applicable), or (c) named subprocessors listed in schedule X. We will not whitelist a blanket EU/UK-only restriction because some backbone infrastructure and CDN/egress endpoints are US-based; however, we will commit that no personal data will be routed to a subprocessor outside those bounds without 30 days' notice and Borealis' ability to object on reasonable grounds. For high-risk categories (e.g., patient genetic identifiers), we will require prior written approval before any processing.

2) UK Addendum redline and DPA: attached is Redwood's redline of the UK Addendum and the DPA (redwood-dpa-v4.docx). We will return both as clean copies by COB Monday (21 Jun) with DocuSign links.

3) Audit and TOMS: Redwood accepts remote audits annually; on-site audits are allowed with 6 weeks' notice and scoping. Our TOMS are included in Annex 2 of the DPA; we will provide SOC 2 Type II report and encryption attestations on request (we have a current SOC 2 report and can share via secure link).

4) Next steps: If Borealis confirms acceptance of Module 2 + UK Addendum redline, we'll prepare the signature package and issue the DocuSign envelope for both the DPA and the SCCs. Proposed signoff timeline: signatures by 2027-06-24 to meet pilot schedule.

Regards,
